A1.justification: Both readable 20-page PDFs describe the same H-ESIM work. Pages 2–20 have identical text, content streams, and rendered appearance; page 1 differs only in publication metadata. Both end with references and contain no appendix pages or embedded supplements, despite citing Appendices B–D. Those unavailable appendices cannot be assessed; the judgments concern the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original sensor-noise calibration measurements, parameter-stability experiments, and video interpolation and deblurring evaluations in Section 6, Figures 4–7, and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original calibration, parameter-stability, interpolation, and deblurring results in Section 6, Figures 4–7, and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Sections 3–5 retain identical APS/EVS noise models, calibration procedures, and H-ESIM simulation steps. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GEN2 and Eiger sensors, calibration captures, high-speed videos, public datasets, and real-data interpolation and deblurring tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains TimeLens, CBMNet, TimeLens-XL, and HR-INR with the same simulator comparisons. Table 2 retains eSL, MAER, and EFNet with the same without/with H-ESIM comparisons.

E3.justification: The one-frame-skipping interpolation protocol, rolling-shutter reference frames, fine-tuning comparisons, and evaluation metrics remain identical. No experimental settings or testing procedures are revised.

E4.justification: The supplied PDFs retain identical noise-distribution, brightness-dependence, polarity, parameter-stability, and qualitative reconstruction analyses in Section 6 and Figures 4–7.

E5.justification: Figure 7 reports the same 200 independent runs with random initialization, parameter-distribution boxplots, and coefficient-of-variation summaries. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All supplied numerical and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains Eiger HR-INR with H-ESIM PSNR of 35.2425, and Table 2 retains eSL with H-ESIM CLIP-IQA of 0.4346.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, the Gaussian and independence assumptions, Taylor approximation, Q-function reasoning, and calibration derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified hybrid-sensor noise modeling, calibration, H-ESIM, and simulation-to-real transfer. The acceptance notice adds no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning sensor-layout noise and reduced simulation-to-real gaps are identical. The rolling-shutter qualification and limitations concerning very low illumination, extreme temperatures, and bandwidth constraints are also retained.

D1.justification: The supplied implementation disclosures remain identical, including NumPy/PyTorch, a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, high-speed input specifications, and the project link. The updated arXiv version link does not change code or data access.

R1.justification: Section 2, the novelty positioning against prior noise models and simulators, and all 84 reference entries are identical. The ECCV acceptance notice does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds a two-line ECCV 2026 acceptance notice and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The title, authors, scientific prose, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page gains an acceptance notice above the title and an updated marginal arXiv stamp. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of pages 2–20 are identical.

improvement.justification: Within the supplied PDFs, v3 changes only publication metadata. The methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations are identical, so the acceptance notice establishes no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality. Referenced appendices are absent from both files.
